question.instructions: Which visual defect does this rendered slide show? Judge only what the image shows, using the deck facts beside it. Do not invent defects: wording, facts, the choice of layout and matters of taste are not defects, and a slide does not need more images, icons or text than it has. Choose none for a slide a careful designer would deliver as it is.

options.none: The slide is clean: none of the other options applies.
options.crowded: Text or parts are packed so densely that the slide is hard to read: long paragraphs filling their boxes, lines squeezed together, parts touching.
options.imbalanced_layout: Parts that belong in one row or grid are out of line with each other, spacing is visibly uneven, or a large empty area sits beside content squeezed to one side.
options.weak_hierarchy: The title is not the most prominent text on the slide, being smaller, lighter or fainter than the body, or emphasis is spread so evenly that nothing leads the eye.
options.unreadable_chart: A chart is squashed or too small to read, or its bars, points, labels or axis overlap, are cut off or cannot be read.
options.poor_image_or_icon_use: An image or icon is stretched, blurry, or plainly unrelated to the text it stands beside.
options.off_theme_styling: A background, text color or title style breaks from the deck theme in the facts: a color outside the theme palette, or a title whose size, weight or alignment differs from the theme's titles.
options.other_visual: Another visual defect you can point to in the image, such as parts drawn over each other. Not wording, facts, layout choice or taste.

fixer.instructions:
You repair the visual design of one slide in a deck written with an HTML slide kit. You get the slide's <section> source, an image of how it renders, what a visual reviewer saw in it (defect kinds with the reviewer's probability for each) and defects the kit measured. Return the whole <section>, rewritten so those defects are gone.

Rules:
- Fix the layout and presentation: choose another data-layout that suits the content, rearrange or regroup parts, remove style attributes, swap a data-icon for one that fits, use the kit's classes. The kit already styles every part well; a style attribute is almost always the cause of a defect, not its fix.
- Keep each content part in the form it has: a table stays a table, a chart stays a chart of the same kind, a picture stays a picture. The request may have asked for that form.
- Keep the words, numbers and chart data exactly as they are, and add no words of your own, not even a label or a heading. Shorten or split text only when no layout change can fix the defect.
- Fix only what the findings name. Leave a part that is fine as it is.
- Use only the layouts and parts in the kit guide. Keep the speaker notes.
